output.headline: Favourable contract terms put Pattinson in pole position for Bond
output.standfirst: Reports that the star – the most high-profile of the final five contenders – has been offered favourable terms hint that Amazon MGM may want him as its first 007
output.bodyHtml:
Robert Pattinson has emerged as the favourite to succeed Daniel Craig as James Bond, according to a credible film-industry source.

Writing in Puck, Matthew Belloni suggests that the favourable contract terms he says have been offered to Pattinson point to the actor, currently in cinemas with reality-crime thriller Primetime, being studio Amazon MGM’s preferred choice for the role.

Related: Robert Pattinson has auditioned for James Bond – and finally the 007 race is interesting | Sian Cain

According to Belloni, while other actors on the shortlist were required to commit to four Bond films, Pattinson’s contract called for three – and offered a much larger (unspecified) fee.

According to Belloni, “it suggests the studio is willing or even eager to sacrifice a bit to get a ‘name’ star to front its most important franchise”.

Producers have run the casting process for the new Bond film, the 26th in the official series, very publicly in recent weeks, with industry reports suggesting that three actors – Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Josh O’Connor – were on the producers’ shortlist, and two weeks later that two others, Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult, were also being tested.

Each contender will have been offered terms before the test process began – what Belloni calls “test deals” – and Belloni suggests producers brought in more established names because they were not fully satisfied with the original three-strong shortlist.

Related: ‘It was a train wreck! I was terrified’: how the new James Bond will be announced – and what can go wrong

Bond 26 will be the first film made by the series’ new owner, Amazon MGM, which has “creative control” of the franchise after striking a deal with its previous producers, Eon, in 2025.

Producers David Heyman and Amy Pascal are overseeing the project, while Dune’s Denis Villeneuve will direct and Peaky Blinders’ Steven Knight is writing the script.

Having starred in franchises including Twilight, Harry Potter, The Batman and Dune, and in acclaimed dramas such as Bel Ami, Cosmopolis, The Lost City of Z and The Lighthouse, Pattinson is the most high-profile of the contenders – something that would have likely counted against him when Eon was still in control, whose credo was that Bond was a bigger star than any actor.

Belloni suggests that in the current media landscape, that may no longer hold: “No franchise is bulletproof any more – everything is vulnerable and most can be helped by a value-add element, like an established star.”
